title: Tensorization of pairing estimates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let each $\Omega_i$ be finite, and let $w_i:\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ and $k_i:\Omega_i\times\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative. Let $p,r\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le p$ and $1\le r$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and every pair of real-valued functions $u,v$ on $\Omega_i$, $\sum_{x,y}k_i(x,y)u(x)v(y)\le\left(\sum_xw_i(x)|u(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}\left(\sum_yw_i(y)|v(y)|^r\right)^{1/r}$. Then for all real-valued $f,g$ on $\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\sum_{x,y}\left(\prod_i k_i(x_i,y_i)\right)f(x)g(y)\le\left(\sum_x\left(\prod_iw_i(x_i)\right)|f(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}\left(\sum_y\left(\prod_iw_i(y_i)\right)|g(y)|^r\right)^{1/r}$.
hypotheses_covered: Each coordinate set Ω_i is finite
The stated one-coordinate pairing inequality holds for every coordinate and every pair of real-valued functions on that coordinate set
f and g are real-valued on the product of the coordinate sets
replaced: Let $\Omega_i$ be finite sets, $w_i(a)\ge0$ weights, and $k_i(a,b)\ge0$ kernels for $i\in[n]$. For $p,r\ge1$, suppose $\sum_{a,b}k_i(a,b)u(a)v(b)\le\|u\|_{p,w_i}\|v\|_{r,w_i}$ for every coordinate $i$ and real $u,v$. Then $\sum_{x,y}(\prod_i k_i(x_i,y_i))f(x)g(y)\le\|f\|_{p,w}\|g\|_{r,w}$ for all real $f,g$ on $\prod_i\Omega_i$, where $w(x)=\prod_iw_i(x_i)$ and $\|h\|_{s,w}=(\sum_xw(x)|h(x)|^s)^{1/s}$.
